clue.text: Towers at sea

parts.note: read 'towers' not as tall buildings but as things that tow, working out on the water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Towers' is pronounced like tall buildings, but it is really 'tow-ers': boats that pull ships into harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small powerful harbour boats whose job is towing larger vessels.

clue.text: First trip up, carrying rushes from the river?

parts.note: the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, a crossword favourite
a flight is a hasty running away, a rush

explanation.surface: A maiden voyage in a plane loaded with reeds cut from a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushes' looks like riverside reeds, but it means fleeing; a flight from the Test is the wordplay. The TEST is a chalk-stream river in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A new aircraft's first trip into the air is a trial run to prove it flies.

clue.text: Making this bird, on crag, fly off

indicators.note: 'fly off' suggests scattering, so the letters of on crag and fly are sent off into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird of prey launching itself from a rocky crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the nine letters of ON CRAG FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large Arctic falcon, the biggest of its family, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Needs two hands to work, taking turns in the kitchen

definitions.text: Needs two hands to work, taking turns in the kitchen

parts.words: Needs two hands to work, taking turns in the kitchen
parts.note: sounds like a kitchen worker sharing shifts, but describes a baking tool with a handle at each end that revolves as it flattens pastry

explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' suggests shifts on a rota; the tool literally turns over the dough, and 'two hands' are its two handles.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylinder used to flatten dough, held at both ends and rolled over pastry.

clue.text: Old hat is no good when off on such jaunts

parts.note: something old hat is out of fashion, simply out

indicators.note: off signals that the letters of is and the no-good abbreviation go wrong, into a new order

explanation.surface: A dated hat is a poor choice when setting off on day trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a piece of headgear, but it is the phrase for something dated; 'off' is the scrambling signal for the two short pieces that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pleasure trips or excursions are both outings and jaunts.

clue.text: Girl modelling saris in Los Angeles

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the Los Angeles abbreviation
models shape and display things, so the letters of saris are reshaped

explanation.surface: A young woman showing off Indian saris on a catwalk in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelling' looks like a catwalk show, but it scrambles the garment's letters; 'in' then splits the city's two letters around them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: The bar of course

parts.note: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but is about a golf course, whose clubhouse bar is jokingly counted after the eighteen holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' seems to mean 'obviously'; it means belonging to a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' slang for the clubhouse bar, visited after the eighteen holes of a round.

clue.text: Planet left in place on the globe

indicators.note: in sets the left abbreviation within the word for place

parts.note: to place something is to put it
O is a round shape, like a globe

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out where a planet sits on a model globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside PUT, then O is added on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: It was classed as the ninth planet when this puzzle was set, now a dwarf planet.

clue.text: Snare to catch a cow

indicators.note: a net catches things, so it holds the letter a within it

parts.note: a net is a trap or snare

explanation.surface: Setting a trap to capture a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts A inside NET. This sense of the answer is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for an ox or bovine animal, as in neat's-foot oil.

clue.text: Drake's ambition, oddly, to be getting off the boat

indicators.note: oddly says the letters of the two words behave strangely, out of their usual order

parts.note: the possessive here gives all its letters, s included

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake's strange urge to leave his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges all fourteen letters of DRAKES AMBITION, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a ship and going ashore is the act of landing passengers or crew.

clue.text: Inn is brought back — and about time!

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word goes round the time word
brought back says the word is is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An inn at last returns, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns the little word round, and 'about' wraps it round the period of time. This inn is a caravan stop in the Middle East and Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravanserai, a roadside lodging for travellers in Asia, is a kind of inn.

clue.text: Sailor playing a large tuna? It's a small, venomous creature

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: playing suggests fooling about, so the large abbreviation and tuna are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor clowning around with a big fish turns out to have a poisonous pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like an actor on stage but tells you to jumble L with TUNA; the clue's 'a' then closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy spider, venomous though rarely dangerous to people.

clue.text: Getting on with other people makes it safer on train

indicators.note: makes says the letters of it safer on train are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Travelling by rail is safer, so people chat more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges the fourteen letters of IT SAFER ON TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing in a friendly way with others, socialising, is what this word describes.

clue.text: Review of Crete's port abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the possessive here keeps every letter, s included

explanation.surface: An inspection of a Cretan harbour that has been deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like 'deserted' but means 'wildly', rearranging CRETES PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking back over past events, a survey of what has gone before.

clue.text: In public transport, copper held to be a nightmare

indicators.note: held means the words in and bus hold the copper symbol between them

parts.note: taken as written
a bus is public transport
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman detained on a bus finds it a dreadful experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal's chemical symbol, which 'held' places between the two pieces either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus was a demon thought to lie on sleepers; the word also means an oppressive dream.

clue.text: Start eating in first part of play — and get thinner

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the words for the first part of a play

parts.note: a play's first part is act one

indicators.note: start means only the opening letter of the word eating is used

explanation.surface: Begin a diet during the opening act of a play and lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' gives E, and 'in' puts it inside ACT ONE. 'thinner' looks like 'slimmer' but is a noun: a solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: This solvent is used to dilute paints and varnishes, and as nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Round to sing — rare adaption by arranger

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: an adaption changes the form of something, so sing and rare are rearranged

explanation.surface: An arranger's unusual reworking of a sung round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a song sung in canon, but it is just the ring-shaped letter; 'adaption' scrambles the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets things up or puts them in order is an arranger.

clue.text: He'd run amok and died, with so many others

indicators.note: running amok is going wild, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving its letters
taken as written, as part of the mixture
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man went on a rampage and was killed along with many other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amok' rearranges HED + RUN into HUNDRE, and D for 'died' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A number of people is meant: a large round count, ten times ten.

clue.text: Fruit suitable for mother and children

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
sons are children

explanation.surface: Fruit that would suit a mum and her kids.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM, a female parent of an animal, is a common crossword word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dark purple plums, a variety of fruit.

clue.text: Re-organising regiment — million made redundant, rational number remains

indicators.note: reorganising a regiment means rearranging the letters left after the removal
made redundant means removed from the job, so that letter is taken out of the word regiment

explanation.surface: A regiment is restructured, a thousand thousand men sacked, and a sensible number stay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made redundant' removes M from REGIMENT, giving REGIENT, which 'Re-organising' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number is one kind of rational number, a ratio of two whole numbers.

clue.text: This foreigner made topping British prime-minister

indicators.note: topping means beheading, so the first letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: A foreigner who became a top British prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' seems to mean 'excellent', but it means cutting off the head: DISRAELI loses his D.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a Middle Eastern state, someone foreign to Britain.

clue.text: Warmongers into recycling?

parts.note: read 'scrap' as a fight, so dealers in fights, while the real trade is dealing in waste metal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmongers' suggests dealers in fights or scraps; the people meant deal in scrap metal for reuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealers who buy and sell waste metal for reuse.

clue.text: We're taking a trip in this vessel

indicators.note: taking a trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of we're fall out of order

explanation.surface: A group boarding a ship to go travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a trip' looks like a voyage but means a stumble, rearranging WERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or pitcher for water is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: I see a worm cast, it's pestilential

indicators.note: a worm cast is a heap thrown up by a worm, but here cast means the letters are thrown into a new shape

explanation.surface: Spotting a worm cast on the lawn, a gardener calls it a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges the nine letters of I SEE A WORM; 'worm cast' is a camouflage phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilential is used loosely to mean irritating, tiresome or annoying.

clue.text: For this material, student is getting lecture

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'For this material, student is getting lecture' (5), answer LISLE: L (student) + IS accounts for three letters, but nothing gives LE from 'lecture' without an indicator; probably an OCR misread, and no scan or search result gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: For this material, student is getting lecture

clue.text: One of this religious following, Simon and I cart off

indicators.note: off says the letters go off course, landing in a new order

parts.note: the joining word and gives no letters, leaving I and cart

explanation.surface: Someone joining a sect, with Simon carting the narrator away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SIMON + I + CART. The answer is an old adjective for Roman Catholicism.
explanation.definitionFit: A term, often disparaging, describing adherence to the Church of Rome.

clue.text: Does this saw worry its way through?

definitions.text: Does this saw worry its way through?

parts.words: Does this saw worry its way through?
parts.note: a fine-bladed saw for decorative cutting shares its name with a verb for anxiety and for wearing away

explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of 'see', but it is the cutting tool; 'worry' means both being anxious and gnawing through.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw cuts intricate patterns, and to fret is to be anxious or to wear away by rubbing.
